1.q: בִּ⁠שְׁנַ֨ת עֶשְׂרִ֤ים וָ⁠שֶׁ֨בַע֙ שָׁנָ֔ה לְ⁠יָרָבְעָ֖ם מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל מָלַ֛ךְ עֲזַרְיָ֥ה בֶן־אֲמַצְיָ֖ה מֶ֥לֶךְ יְהוּדָֽה
1.note: In this verse and the next two verses, the author is introducing **Azariah** as a participant in the story as the new king of **Judah**. To translate this verse, see how you translated the similar expressions in 8:25.

2.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 8:17. Alternate translation: [He was 16 years old]
See how you translated the similar expression in 14:2. Alternate translation: [was Jekoliah, and she was from Jerusalem]

3.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 1:13. Alternate translation: [And he did what Yahweh considered to be right]

4.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 14:4. Alternate translation: [he did not remove the high places]

5.note: In this context, the word **touched** means that Yahweh “afflicted” Azariah with a disease. (See the discussion in the introduction to this chapter of why Yahweh did that.) You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [And Yahweh afflicted the king with a disease]

6.q: וְ⁠יֶ֛תֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י עֲזַרְיָ֖הוּ וְ⁠כָל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה הֲ⁠לֹא־הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל־סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַ⁠יָּמִ֖ים לְ⁠מַלְכֵ֥י יְהוּדָֽה
6.note: In this verse and the next verse, the author is concluding the story of Azariah. To translate this verse, see how you translated the similar phrases in 1:18.

7.note: See how you translated the same expression in 8:24. Alternate translation: [And Azariah passed away] or [And Azariah died]

Here the author is using the pronoun **they** in a general sense, not to refer to specific people. Use an expression for this that would be natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and people buried him] or [and he was buried]
See how you translated the similar expression in 8:24. Alternate translation: [in the same place where people had buried his ancestors]

8.q: בִּ⁠שְׁנַ֨ת שְׁלֹשִׁ֤ים וּ⁠שְׁמֹנֶה֙ שָׁנָ֔ה לַ⁠עֲזַרְיָ֖הוּ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה מָ֠לַךְ זְכַרְיָ֨הוּ בֶן־יָרָבְעָ֧ם עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל בְּ⁠שֹׁמְר֖וֹן שִׁשָּׁ֥ה חֳדָשִֽׁים
8.note: In this verse and the next verse, the author is introducing **Zechariah** as a participant in the story as the new king of **Israel**. To translate this verse, see how you translated the similar expressions in 8:25 and [13:1](ta:13).

9.q: וַ⁠יַּ֤עַשׂ הָ⁠רַע֙ בְּ⁠עֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה כַּ⁠אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשׂ֖וּ אֲבֹתָ֑י⁠ו לֹ֣א סָ֗ר מֵֽ⁠חַטֹּאות֙ יָרָבְעָ֣ם בֶּן־נְבָ֔ט אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶחֱטִ֖יא אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל
9.note: The author is continuing to introduce Zechariah. See how you translated the similar expressions in 3:3 and 8:18. Alternate translation: [And he did what Yahweh considered to be evil. He did not stop committing the same sins as Jeroboam, the son of Nebat, who had caused Israel to sin]

10.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 3:24. Alternate translation: [and he attacked him]

11.q: וְ⁠יֶ֖תֶר דִּבְרֵ֣י זְכַרְיָ֑ה הִנָּ֣⁠ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל־סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַ⁠יָּמִ֖ים לְ⁠מַלְכֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל
11.note: In this verse and the next verse, the author is concluding the story of Zechariah. To translate this verse, see how you translated the similar phrases in 1:18.

12.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 1:7. Alternate translation: [It was the message that Yahweh had spoken to Jehu]

12.q: בְּנֵ֣י רְבִיעִ֔ים יֵשְׁב֥וּ לְ⁠ךָ֖ עַל־כִּסֵּ֣א יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל
12.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 10:30. Alternate translation: [Four generations of your descendants will succeed you as the king of Israel]

13.q: שַׁלּ֤וּם בֶּן־יָבֵישׁ֙ מָלַ֔ךְ בִּ⁠שְׁנַ֨ת שְׁלֹשִׁ֤ים וָ⁠תֵ֨שַׁע֙ שָׁנָ֔ה לְ⁠עֻזִיָּ֖ה מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה וַ⁠יִּמְלֹ֥ךְ יֶֽרַח־יָמִ֖ים בְּ⁠שֹׁמְרֽוֹן
13.note: In this verse, the author is introducing **Shallum** as a participant in the story as the new king of **Israel**. See how you translated the similar expressions in 8:25.

14.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 1:3. Alternate translation: [And Menahem, the son of Gadi, came]
See how you translated the similar expression in 3:24. Alternate translation: [And he attacked Shallum]

15.q: וְ⁠יֶ֨תֶר֙ דִּבְרֵ֣י שַׁלּ֔וּם וְ⁠קִשְׁר֖⁠וֹ אֲשֶׁ֣ר קָשָׁ֑ר הִנָּ֣⁠ם כְּתֻבִ֗ים עַל־סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַ⁠יָּמִ֖ים לְ⁠מַלְכֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל
15.note: In this verse, the author is concluding the story of Shallum. To translate it, see how you translated the similar phrases in 1:18.
See how you translated the similar expression in 12:20. Alternate translation: [and the conspiracy that he carried out]

16.q: אָ֣ז יַכֶּֽה־מְ֠נַחֵם אֶת־תִּפְסַ֨ח וְ⁠אֶת־כָּל־אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֤⁠הּ וְ⁠אֶת־גְּבוּלֶ֨י⁠הָ֙ מִ⁠תִּרְצָ֔ה כִּ֛י לֹ֥א פָתַ֖ח
16.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these phrases, since the second phrase gives the reason for the result that the first phrase describes. Alternate translation: [Then, because one did not open, Menahem struck Tiphsah and all who were in it and its borders, from Tirzah]

16.q: אָ֣ז יַכֶּֽה־מְ֠נַחֵם אֶת־תִּפְסַ֨ח וְ⁠אֶת־כָּל־אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֤⁠הּ וְ⁠אֶת־גְּבוּלֶ֨י⁠הָ֙ מִ⁠תִּרְצָ֔ה
16.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information that Menahem began this military campaign **from Tirzah** at the beginning of the sentence. Alternate translation: [Then from Tirzah Menahem struck Tiphsah and all who were in it and its borders]
See how you translated the similar expression in 3:19. Alternate translation: [Then Menahem destroyed Tiphsah]
See how you translated the similar expression in 10:32. Alternate translation: [and the surrounding territory]

Here the author is using the pronoun **one** in a general sense, not to refer to a specific person. Use an expression for this that would be natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the people of the city refused to open its gates and admit him]

The author is using the action of not opening the city gates for Menahem to represent refusing to accept him as king. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the people of the city refused to accept him as their king]
See how you translated the similar expression in 3:23. Alternate translation: [And he killed all the people of the city]

17.q: בִּ⁠שְׁנַ֨ת שְׁלֹשִׁ֤ים וָ⁠תֵ֨שַׁע֙ שָׁנָ֔ה לַ⁠עֲזַרְיָ֖ה מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה מָ֠לַךְ מְנַחֵ֨ם בֶּן־גָּדִ֧י עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל עֶ֥שֶׂר שָׁנִ֖ים בְּ⁠שֹׁמְרֽוֹן
17.note: In this verse and the next verse, the author is introducing **Menahem** as a participant in the story as the new king of **Israel**. To translate this verse, see how you translated the similar expressions in 8:25 and [13:1](ta:13).

18.q: וַ⁠יַּ֥עַשׂ הָ⁠רַ֖ע בְּ⁠עֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה לֹ֣א סָ֠ר מֵ⁠עַ֨ל חַטֹּ֜אות יָרָבְעָ֧ם בֶּן־נְבָ֛ט אֲשֶׁר־הֶחֱטִ֥יא אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל כָּל־יָמָֽי⁠ו
18.note: The author is continuing to introduce Menahem. See how you translated the similar expressions in 3:3 and 8:18. Alternate translation: [And he did what Yahweh considered to be evil. He did not stop committing the same sins as Jeroboam, the son of Nebat, who had caused Israel to sin, all of his days]

18.q: לֹ֣א סָ֠ר מֵ⁠עַ֨ל חַטֹּ֜אות יָרָבְעָ֧ם בֶּן־נְבָ֛ט אֲשֶׁר־הֶחֱטִ֥יא אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל כָּל־יָמָֽי⁠ו
18.note: If it would be more natural in your language, before the information that Menahem **did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam**, you may want to put the information that Menahem did that **all of his days**. Alternate translation: [All of his days, he did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam, the son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin]

19.note: Many interpreters consider **Pul** to be the same king who is known elsewhere as Tiglath Pileser. See what you decided to do in the cases of the Israelite and Judean kings whom the author sometimes calls Jehoram and sometimes calls Joram. If you have decided to use the same names in your translation that the biblical author does in each place, you may wish to use the name Pul here. If you decided to use the same name consistently for a given person, you may wish to use the name Tiglath Pileser here, since that king appears later in this chapter and in chapter 16.
See how you decided to represent the weight of a kikkar of silver in 5:5.
See how you translated the similar expression in 3:10. Alternate translation: [so that Pul would use his power to help him]
See how you translated the similar expression in 14:5. Alternate translation: [so that he would have firmer control of the kingdom]

20.q: וַ⁠יֹּצֵא֩ מְנַחֵ֨ם אֶת־הַ⁠כֶּ֜סֶף עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל עַ֚ל כָּל־גִּבּוֹרֵ֣י הַ⁠חַ֔יִל
20.note: The author is using the preposition **over** in these two instances in order to depict the imposition of a financial burden on or **over** wealthy Israelites. If your language would not use a term comparable to “over” in this way, you could use a preposition that indicated the source of the funds, as many versions do. Alternate translation: [And Menahem exacted the silver from Israel, from all of the mighty of valor]

While in many biblical contexts this expression describes a soldier who can fight powerfully and effectively, the term can also describe a person of great wealth and standing, and that seems to be the meaning in this context. If you have already translated the book of 1 Samuel, see how you translated the similar expression in 1 Samuel 9:1. Alternate translation: [the wealthy citizens]
See how you decided to represent the weight of a shekel at 5:5.

20.q: וַ⁠יָּ֨שָׁב֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר וְ⁠לֹא־עָ֥מַד שָׁ֖ם בָּ⁠אָֽרֶץ
20.note: The author is describing one event before describing another event that preceded it. If it would be helpful your language, you may wish to relate these events in the order in which they happened. Alternate translation: [And the king of Assyria did not stay there in the land. Instead, he returned home]

21.q: וְ⁠יֶ֛תֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י מְנַחֵ֖ם וְ⁠כָל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה הֲ⁠לוֹא־הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל־סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַ⁠יָּמִ֖ים לְ⁠מַלְכֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל
21.note: In this verse and the next verse, the author is concluding the story of Menahem. To translate this verse, see how you translated the similar phrases in 1:18.

22.note: See how you translated the same expression in 8:24. Alternate translation: [And Menahem passed away] or [And Menahem died]

23.q: בִּ⁠שְׁנַת֙ חֲמִשִּׁ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה לַ⁠עֲזַרְיָ֖ה מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה מָ֠לַךְ פְּקַֽחְיָ֨ה בֶן־מְנַחֵ֧ם עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל בְּ⁠שֹׁמְר֖וֹן שְׁנָתָֽיִם
23.note: In this verse and the next verse, the author is introducing **Pekahiah** as a participant in the story as the new king of **Israel**. To translate this verse, see how you translated the similar expressions in 8:25 and [13:1](ta:13).

24.q: וַ⁠יַּ֥עַשׂ הָ⁠רַ֖ע בְּ⁠עֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה לֹ֣א סָ֗ר מֵֽ⁠חַטֹּאות֙ יָרָבְעָ֣ם בֶּן־נְבָ֔ט אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶחֱטִ֖יא אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל
24.note: The author is continuing to introduce Pekahiah. See how you translated the similar expressions in 3:3 and 8:18. Alternate translation: [And he did what Yahweh considered to be evil. He did not stop committing the same sins as Jeroboam, the son of Nebat, who had caused Israel to sin]

25.q: וַ⁠יִּקְשֹׁ֣ר עָלָי⁠ו֩ פֶּ֨קַח בֶּן־רְמַלְיָ֜הוּ שָׁלִישׁ֗⁠וֹ וַ⁠יַּכֵּ֨⁠הוּ בְ⁠שֹׁמְר֜וֹן בְּ⁠אַרְמ֤וֹן בֵּית־מלך אֶת־אַרְגֹּ֣ב וְ⁠אֶת־הָ⁠אַרְיֵ֔ה וְ⁠עִמּ֛⁠וֹ חֲמִשִּׁ֥ים אִ֖ישׁ מִ⁠בְּנֵ֣י גִלְעָדִ֑ים
25.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information that Pekah also “struck” Argob and Arieh with the information that he **struck** the king and the information that **50 men of the sons of the Gileadites** were **with him** with the information that Pekah **conspired against** Pekahiah. Alternate translation: [And Pekah, the son of Remaliah, his captain, and with him 50 men of the sons of the Gileadites, conspired against him, and in Samaria, in the citadel of the house of the king, he struck him, Argob, and Arieh]
See how you translated the similar expression in 3:24. Alternate translation: [and he attacked him]
See how you translated the similar expression in 8:12. Alternate translation: [men who were Gileadites]

26.q: וְ⁠יֶ֛תֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י פְקַחְיָ֖ה וְ⁠כָל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה הִנָּ֣⁠ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל־סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַ⁠יָּמִ֖ים לְ⁠מַלְכֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל
26.note: The author is concluding the story of Pekahiah. See how you translated the similar phrases in 1:18.

27.q: בִּ⁠שְׁנַ֨ת חֲמִשִּׁ֤ים וּ⁠שְׁתַּ֨יִם֙ שָׁנָ֔ה לַ⁠עֲזַרְיָ֖ה מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה מָ֠לַךְ פֶּ֣קַח בֶּן־רְמַלְיָ֧הוּ עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל בְּ⁠שֹׁמְר֖וֹן עֶשְׂרִ֥ים שָׁנָֽה
27.note: In this verse and the next verse, the author is introducing **Pekah** as a participant in the story as the new king of **Israel**. To translate this verse, see how you translated the similar expressions in 8:25 and [13:1](ta:13).

28.q: וַ⁠יַּ֥עַשׂ הָ⁠רַ֖ע בְּ⁠עֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה לֹ֣א סָ֗ר מִן־חַטֹּאות֙ יָרָבְעָ֣ם בֶּן־נְבָ֔ט אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶחֱטִ֖יא אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל
28.note: The author is continuing to introduce Pekah. See how you translated the similar expressions in 3:2 and 8:18. Alternate translation: [And he did what Yahweh considered to be evil. He did not stop committing the same sins as Jeroboam, the son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin]

29.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 8:20. Alternate translation: [During the reign of Pekah]

The pronoun **them** refers to the people of the cities and regions the author has just listed. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [and he exiled the people who lived in those areas]

30.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 12:20. Alternate translation: [And Hoshea, the son of Elah, formed a conspiracy]
See how you translated the similar expression in 3:24. Alternate translation: [and he attacked him]

If your language would not represent a number in a form such as **20**, you could represent this number in a form that your language would use. Alternate translation: [in the twentieth year of Jotham]

**Uzziah** is another name for Azariah, whose reign the author describes in [15:1–7](ta:15). The author calls this same king Azariah in verses 32 and 34. If you have decided to use the same names in your translation that the biblical author does in each place, you may wish to use the name Uzziah here. If you have decided to use the same name consistently for a given person, you may wish to use the name Azariah here.

31.q: וְ⁠יֶ֥תֶר דִּבְרֵי־פֶ֖קַח וְ⁠כָל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה הִנָּ֣⁠ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל־סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַ⁠יָּמִ֖ים לְ⁠מַלְכֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל
31.note: The author is concluding the story of Pekah. See how you translated the similar phrases in 1:18.

32.q: בִּ⁠שְׁנַ֣ת שְׁתַּ֔יִם לְ⁠פֶ֥קַח בֶּן־רְמַלְיָ֖הוּ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל מָלַ֛ךְ יוֹתָ֥ם בֶּן־עֻזִיָּ֖הוּ מֶ֥לֶךְ יְהוּדָֽה
32.note: In this verse and the next two verses, the author is introducing **Jotham** as a participant in the story as the new king of **Judah**. To translate this verse, see how you translated the similar expressions in 8:16.

If your language would not describe a year of a king’s reign in a form such as **the year of two**, you could represent this year in a form that your language would use. Alternate translation: [In the second year of Pekah]

33.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 8:17. Alternate translation: [He was 25 years old]

35.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 14:4. Alternate translation: [he did not remove the high places]
See how you translated the similar expression in 14:22. Alternate translation: [He was the one who built]
See how you translated the similar expression in 5:18. Alternate translation: [the temple of Yahweh]

The author assumes that readers will understand that by **the house of Yahweh**, he means the courtyard around the temple, into which this **gate** led. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the courtyard of Yahweh’s temple]

36.q: וְ⁠יֶ֛תֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י יוֹתָ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה הֲ⁠לֹא־הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל־סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַ⁠יָּמִ֖ים לְ⁠מַלְכֵ֥י יְהוּדָֽה
36.note: In this verse and the next two verses, the author is concluding the story of Jotham. To translate this verse, see how you translated the similar phrases in 1:18.

37.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 3:6. Alternate translation: [At that time]

38.note: See how you translated the same expression in 8:24. Alternate translation: [And Jotham passed away] or [And Jotham died]

The expression **was buried** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and people buried him]
See how you translated the similar expression in 8:24. Alternate translation: [with his ancestors … his ancestor] or [in the same place where people had buried his ancestors … his ancestor]
